verdict: Reddit grew revenue 53% to $895M on surging ad sales and kept $283M as profit — the forum site now draws 130 million daily users and has a money machine to match.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's thousands of communities — 95% of everything Reddit earns.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Mostly licensing Reddit's vast archive of human conversation to AI companies for training data, plus premium subscriptions.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform, its ad system and AI tools — Reddit's biggest cost line, up 34% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling ads to brands and agencies — up 63% YoY as the ad business scales.

takeaways.title: Ads are booming
takeaways.text: Ad revenue rose 54% to $847M as brands pay up to reach Reddit's communities — and data licensing to AI companies added most of the other $48M.

takeaways.title: Daily users hit a record
takeaways.text: Daily active uniques rose 12% to 130.3 million, and weekly users reached 515.2 million — a bigger audience to sell ads against every quarter.

takeaways.title: 45 cents of every dollar
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was $402M — 45% of revenue — and free cash flow was $363M. Reddit also joined the S&P 500 index this quarter.

otherDetail: Other income of $28M, net — mostly interest earned on Reddit's $3.0B pile of cash and marketable securities.
